PLP1-related leukodystrophy; optic atrophy occurs in 30–79%. Bowel and bladder symptoms reflect neurologic dysfunction without established local injury.
Progressive renal tubulointerstitial injury. Anemia is secondary to renal failure; retinal pigmentation alone does not establish damaging retinal disease across this umbrella.
Subclavian venous compression and effort thrombosis define this vascular thoracic outlet syndrome.
Complement factor D deficiency causes impaired antibacterial immunity and recurrent Neisseria infections; no consistent organ injury is established.
Arterial disease, bone fragility and cutis laxa define the syndrome; hydronephrosis in 4/6. Seizures in 2/6 omitted at cap; retinal vessel tortuosity alone does not establish eye damage.
In situ carcinoma occupies the ureter, which belongs to the renal axis.
Defined by complex central nervous system developmental dysfunction; associated congenital malformations have no specified consistent organ distribution.
Anterior horn motor neuron disease; facioscapulohumeral muscle wasting reflects denervation rather than direct muscle pathology.
Inherited phagocyte oxidative-burst defect affects leukocyte function and immunity. Site-specific infections are separate diagnoses; direct granulomatous organ injury lacks frequencies.
Congenital motor pathway disorder producing involuntary mirror movements; no other organ disease is established.
Acquired transmissible prion infection causes progressive spongiform brain degeneration.
Neurodevelopmental and brain abnormalities, cleft palate (3/5), and clubfeet (30–79%) characterize the syndrome. Pulmonary hypoplasia is 2/7; heart-defect frequency is unestablished.
Defined congenital dystroglycanopathy combines muscular dystrophy, major brain malformations/leukodystrophy and eye anomalies; individual eye findings have variable frequencies.
Ulceration directly damages the esophageal wall; no specific infectious or immune mechanism is inherent to the concept.
Neuronal ceroid lipofuscin storage disorder causes progressive neurodegeneration. Vascular storage material alone does not establish cardiovascular dysfunction.
Inborn glutamine metabolism disorders; major neurodevelopmental dysfunction is characteristic across both listed deficiency subtypes and affects most patients.
Hereditary peripheral neuropathy; distal weakness and wasting arise from denervation, without established direct disease of another organ.
Germ cell tumor arising in the ovary, a reproductive organ outside the axes; endocrine gland dysfunction is not defining.
Congenital ptosis, lens dislocation and high myopia define the syndrome; structural fingernail dysplasia occurs in 30–79%.
Inherited factor VIII excess is a coagulation disorder. DVT and pulmonary embolism are separately diagnosed thrombotic diseases; single-case organ complications do not justify added axes.
Neurodevelopmental disorder with heart defects and unilateral renal agenesis described as common; exact rates unavailable. Unspecified eye anomalies do not establish damaging ocular disease.
Skeletal dysplasia with bowed shortened bones, abnormal metaphyses, vertebral changes and joint restriction; narrow thorax alone does not establish pulmonary injury.
The defining syndrome combines hypotrichosis, nail dysplasia and hyperkeratosis with kyphoscoliosis and cataract.
Intellectual disability and developmental delay are principal features. Clefting and cardiac, skeletal and renal anomalies lack evidence of involvement in at least 30%.
